explain.say: Electricity! In 1752 Benjamin Franklin flew a kite in a storm to show it. Do not ever try that! Then look at 1800: Alessandro Volta in Italy stacked metal discs with salty wet card and made the first battery. Can you find the magnet?

explain.say: In 1831 Michael Faraday found that moving a magnet near a coil of wire makes electricity flow. That is how almost all power stations still work! Look at 1879: Joseph Swan in England and Thomas Edison in America made light bulbs that glowed for hours.

faq.a: No single person. The Greek thinker Thales noticed static electricity around 600 BCE, and many scientists, like Franklin, Volta and Faraday, discovered more over the centuries.
Alessandro Volta in Italy, in 1800. His voltaic pile was a stack of zinc and copper discs with card soaked in salty water between them. The volt is named after him.

faq.q: When did homes first get electricity?
faq.a: In the 1880s, the first power stations in London and New York sent electricity to nearby streets and buildings. Many villages and towns got it much later.

faq.q: How does a generator make electricity?
faq.a: Spinning a magnet near coils of wire, or a coil near a magnet, pushes electric current through the wire. Michael Faraday discovered this in 1831.

faq.q: Where does the word electricity come from?
faq.a: From the Greek word elektron, which means amber, because rubbing amber makes static electricity.

facts: Alessandro Volta built the first electric battery, the voltaic pile, in 1800.
Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, the idea behind generators, in 1831.
The word electricity comes from elektron, the Greek word for amber.
